<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-flow-node-writes.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b1411d4a7aa6eb5880625a7cfa42276d8626824` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `019095fdff731f7e957d2116ffe4df874509056e` — the merge of head `7093e465ece700be57375a8a77bb37deec69cb5c` into base `0b1411d4a7aa6eb5880625a7cfa42276d8626824`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 019095fdff731f7e957d2116ffe4df874509056e && git checkout 019095fdff731f7e957d2116ffe4df874509056e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b1411d4a7aa6eb5880625a7cfa42276d8626824 7093e465ece700be57375a8a77bb37deec69cb5c && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b1411d4a7aa6eb5880625a7cfa42276d8626824 && git merge --no-ff 7093e465ece700be57375a8a77bb37deec69cb5c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b1411d4a7aa6eb5880625a7cfa42276d8626824
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b1411d4a7aa6eb5880625a7cfa42276d8626824` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4e9c077b1cf03c0573b5509b1bfef517fb6fea92`
Local-runs: none

PR #37491 (card #36964), declaration face. Read: the card body and its four comments (two triage notes, the claim 7186576390, the os-dev report 7187822605), follow-up card #37504, the PR body, the net diff against `main` (5 files, +528/−12) and the check-runs on the head (57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed). Nothing was built or run; every statement about behaviour below is from reading the code.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `os validate` / `os lint` / `os compile` / `os build` and of the runtime publish gate: NARROWED. The PR declares it unchanged. Wrong.** `flow-condition-option-label` stays `error` and now fires at five positions it never read: `get_record` / `update_record` / `delete_record` `filter` operands, `timeRelative.filter` operands, edge `condition`, `decision` `conditions[].expression`. A flow that validated and published on `main` is refused on this head. The changeset says so itself ("an active flow write carrying one of these is refused there too"), and so does the PR body's maintainer summary.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/lint`: unchanged. Right.** `flow-select-options.ts` is imported only by the two validator modules and is re-exported by no entry (`index.ts`, `runtime.ts` and `rule-explanations.ts` are untouched). `FieldReads`, `TRIGGER_RECORD_READS` and `optionLabelOperands` are module-internal. No `yes` arm is owed for exports.
- **Rule id: right.** One existing id, no new one. The filter operand belongs to `flow-condition-option-label` and not `flow-node-write-unknown-option`: the write rule's verdict is a validator refusal (`invalid_option`), and nothing refuses a filter operand.
- **Start-condition arm: unchanged. Right.** With the default `TRIGGER_RECORD_READS`, `readOf` builds the same expression as on `main` (optional `record.` / `previous.` root, then the field, then the same lookahead).
- **Resolution parity with the existing arm: holds.** Every new arm reads options through the same `indexSelectOptions` (served objects, tied fields dropped, picklist fields skipped, a label that is also a value never reported). Per shape:
  - nested `$and` / `$or` / `$not` groups: walked by the spec's own `flowFilterOperands`; the prefix parser accepts any nesting and flips `negated` per `$not`;
  - lookups: a nested-relation condition is not judged (the outer key has no options; a deeper path under a select field fails the operator check);
  - multi-select: judged as a label that no stored code equals; `$in` / `$nin` members judged one by one;
  - dynamic values: a CEL envelope, a non-string operand and any string holding a brace are skipped; a condition's variable or template comparand is not a quoted label;
  - `get_record` rows: only `limit` absent or 1, which matches the executor's `findOne` branch (a truthy `limit` above 1 is the list branch).
- **Throw on malformed input: none found.** Every member access is guarded; `collectFlowGraphs` hands out record members only; `flowFilterOperands` is cycle-safe.
- **False positives: one found, S1 below.** The rest of the cases asked about (option value equal to its label, variable or template values, formula expressions) are silent by construction.

Findings:

- **M1 (must-fix) — the declaration is a false `no` and the level is one step low.** The diff narrows a published accept set at `error`, so it owes:
  - `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset (no export is added, so not `yes`);
  - `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a value an author could write is now refused);
  - `'@objectstack/lint': minor`, not `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor`);
  - a `**BREAKING**` banner with the FROM → TO mapping (`filter: { stage: 'Closed Lost' }` → `{ stage: 'closed_lost' }`; `deal.stage == 'Closed Lost'` → `deal.stage == 'closed_lost'`) and the CEL-envelope escape, plus `!` in the title;
  - an ADR-0087 disposition marker in the changeset. The fitting one is `not-required (already-registered publish-refuses-flows-that-save-and-do-not-run)`, with that entry's `surface` extended: today it says "a start condition that compares a select field with one of its option labels";
  - a PR-body `Skills-docs: follow-up #37504` line, owed by any kind other than `none`.

  Precedent on `main`, all four the same shape:
  - `.changeset/35143-flow-publish-checks-second-batch.md` introduced this very rule: `minor`, `fix(lint)!`, `(narrowing)`, `narrowed`, BREAKING, registered entry.
  - `.changeset/36237-hop-list-equality.md` is the exact analogue, an existing refusal extended to one more site: `minor`, `(narrowing)`, `narrowed`, BREAKING, `not-required (already-registered …)` with the entry's surface extended.
  - `.changeset/34776-publish-checks-build-probes.md` and `.changeset/36167-cel-list-equality-refused.md`: the same.

  Counter-precedent: none found. The `@objectstack/lint` `patch` + `Metadata-protocol: none` changesets on `main` that mention a refusal are warnings (#36052, #36202), wording (#34694, #35734) or the removal of a false positive (#36545). None widens an `error` rule's coverage.

  The green `Check Changeset` and ADR-0087 gates do not contradict this: they read the declaration as written and cannot judge its direction.

- **S1 (should-fix) — a rebound `record` / `previous` is still read as the trigger row.** `optionLabelsBeyondStart` builds `shadowed` for BARE reads only; the roots `record` and `previous` are never dropped. The row-variable loop skips a `get_record` whose `outputVariable` is `record`, but the trigger reader still judges `record.F` against the trigger object. So a flow that binds `record` to another object's row (`get_record` `outputVariable: 'record'`, a loop `iteratorVariable: 'record'`, an assignment) is refused when its condition compares a literal that is a label on the trigger object's field and a value on the other object's same-named field (`status`: `Open` as a label on one, a plain-string option on the other). A valid flow is refused at `error`. Low probability; the fix is to drop a root that `collectFlowVariableNames` reports as bound. No test covers it.

- **S2 (should-fix) — four new read paths have no test.**
  - An edge or `decision` branch inside a region (loop body, parallel branch): `graphHolder` and the nested path text are exercised by nothing; the edge and decision ablations hit the top-level graph only.
  - `$not`, `$nin` and `$and`: the `negated` parity (`$not` over `$ne`) and two of the four equality operators are unpinned.
  - A condition on a time-relative flow's trigger record (`sweptObject` as `triggerObject`), and `previous.F`.
  - The ambiguity drop when two `get_record` steps bind one variable to different objects, and the node-id and screen-field shadows.

  What is covered: each of the six positions has a refused case; the silent controls sit on the `get_record` filter and on the edge condition, which share code with the other positions.

- **N1 (nit) — top-level node indices can shift on a malformed flow.** The flow handed to `collectFlowGraphs` has `nodes: recordsOf(flow.nodes)`, so a non-record member ahead of a container renumbers the top-level index in `graph.path`, and `graphHolder` then walks the AUTHORED list with it: the wrong holder, or none. A map-form `nodes` resolves to no holder. No throw; a missed or misplaced finding on input the schema refuses anyway.
- **N2 (nit) — the `readonly` select reading is in the PR body only.** A row of a readonly select is judged by shape, so it can hold a non-option string. The changeset should say the field is still judged here, and that an edge or decision condition has no envelope escape (only a filter operand does).
- **N3 (nit) — label drift.** The `optionLabelsBeyondStart` docblock calls itself "(1-iii)"; its call site is "1-iv", and 1-iii is the start-condition block.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: the PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: no` with `Metadata-protocol: none`, on a `patch`. Wrong on all three; see M1. Owed: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `minor`, BREAKING banner, FROM → TO, ADR-0087 marker.

Two consequences for the seat:

- The corrected declaration moves the PR to the narrowing face, which is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with a ④ design judgment over the whole non-prose diff. This record is rendered at `TIER_DEFAULT` on the declaration face, as briefed. It cannot be the PASS of the corrected head.
- Extending the ADR-0087 entry edits `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.publish-refuses-flows-that-save-and-do-not-run.ts` and the generated registry. That is outside the claim's file surface and is a published-spec path, so the seat widens the fence or rules another disposition.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (tests in the shared harness `flow-publish-checks-second-batch.test.ts`): accepted.
- Dev deviation 2 (only `flow-condition-option-label` extended): accepted; see ①.
- Dev deviation 3 (`delete_record`, `timeRelative.filter` and `decision` branches beyond the card's three shapes): in family and derived from the spec ledger. Accepted as scope; each one is part of the narrowing M1 names.
- Dev deviation 4 (PR footer form): no contract effect.
- Open question 1 (the automation skill's trap sentence, `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` §4): answered A. #37504 is the right carrier: `skills/**` is governed and fenced off an implementation card, the card is `Blocked-by: #37491`, and the stale sentence under-promises (it says "never checked") for the gap between the two merges. Owed with it: the `Skills-docs: follow-up #37504` line (M1).
- Open question 2 (`FLOW_CONDITION_OPTION_LABEL_EXPLANATION`, "why a start condition compares option values"): answered A. Verified: PR #37422 is open and its file list holds `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts` and `index.ts`. #37504 is the right carrier. Until it lands, `os explain` describes a narrower rule than the one that fired.
- #37504 does not list the third stale text, the ADR-0087 entry's `surface`. That one rides this PR under M1, not the follow-up.
- Out-of-scope item 3 (positions left unjudged: a time-relative start's own `config.condition`, node-level `config.condition`, `NODE_ID.record.F`, a loop iterator over a list read, nested relations): no carrier, stated in the PR body. Accepted; each is a missed finding, not a wrong one.
- Security: not security-touching. No changed hunk reads or changes authentication, permissions, sharing, secrets or a trust boundary; the dev's `security_findings: none` holds. The declaration-face record carries no `Security-touching:` machine line, so this is stated here.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff issues no query and materialises no ids; it reads authored metadata only.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- Check-runs on the head: 57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, read from the API.
